Concentration name: Literature and the Arts, Social Sciences, History, Development and Urban Studies, and Gender and Sexuality
description: The Department of African American Studies is an intellectual community committed to producing, refining and helping to expand the knowledge base about people of African descent in the United States, the Caribbean, Latin America, and Africa. In keeping with the University of California's mission of 'teaching, research and public service,' our department offers a rigorous and multi-disciplinary undergraduate and graduate curriculum that aims to help students: Examine and analyze the historical, cultural, and social complexities of the African American experience; Develop the critical and analytical skills needed to understand the nuances of the African Diaspora; and Prepare for leadership and service in a global society.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies

description: American Studies is a diverse, rigorous, and interdisciplinary program that encourages students to design an individual course of study that investigates the history, culture, and society of the United States. In the major, students choose an area of concentration to pursue based on their individual interests. Students often focus on themes such as: racial and ethnic identities; gender and sexuality; media and popular culture; law and politics; and the United States in a global context.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies

description: The Ancient Greek and Roman Studies (AGRS) major is designed for students who want to explore the literature and culture of the ancient Mediterranean world in all its depth and range, but who prefer to do so without the intensive language requirements of the Classics or Classical Languages majors. The AGRS major provides an expansive introduction to the history, literature, and culture of the ancient world. Students will engage with a broad range of topics from different regions and time periods, and they will study a variety of primary sources, including literature, inscriptions, material culture, and art. The program also emphasizes the development of critical thinking, research, and writing skills. Many AGRS majors choose to double-major in another field, such as History, Philosophy, Art History, or English.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Greek and Roman Studies

description: Anthropology is the study of human beings, past and present. To understand the full sweep and complexity of cultures across all of human history, anthropology draws and builds upon knowledge from the social and biological sciences as well as the humanities and physical sciences. A central concern of anthropologists is the application of knowledge to the solution of human problems. Historically, anthropologists in the United States have been trained in one of four areas: sociocultural anthropology, biological/physical anthropology, archaeology, and linguistics. Anthropologists often integrate the perspectives of several of these areas into their research, teaching, and professional lives.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology

Concentration name: Statistics, Numerical Analysis, Physics, Physical Sciences, Economics, Computer Science, Operations Research, Mathematical Biology
description: The Department of Mathematics offers an undergraduate major in Applied Mathematics leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The Applied Mathematics major has been designed for students who want to use mathematics to solve problems in other fields. This major is particularly suitable for students who intend to work in industry, or who want to study a field such as economics or physics at the graduate level.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Mathematics

description: The major in architecture leads to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. It combines required courses in environmental design and architecture with opportunities for highly varied individual programs. Through its core courses, the program offers a broad introduction to the field of architecture, and through studies in the various areas it provides opportunities to prepare for specialization in the field in graduate study, or for work in several architecture-related fields. In addition to the course work, students may also take advantage of the college's many resources, including the Architecture Library, the Environmental Design Archives, the CED shop, and the CED computer labs.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Arts with a major in architecture is a pre-professional degree. The National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB) only accredits professional degrees (Master of Architecture). Because the Bachelor of Arts in Architecture is a pre-professional degree, it is not accredited by the NAAB.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Architecture

description: The Art Practice department provides rigorous training in the practice of visual art. Students are expected to develop a clear understanding of the history of art and the relationship of their work to contemporary art. The program focuses on several key areas of art practice: painting, sculpture, printmaking, digital media, photography, and performance. The program provides a rigorous education in the practice of visual art, within the context of a world-class public research university. Art Practice students learn to think critically and creatively, to analyze visual culture, and to communicate through a variety of media.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Art

description: The program in Asian American and Asian Diaspora Studies (AAADS) is an interdisciplinary program that offers a unique perspective on the history, culture, and experiences of people of Asian descent in the United States and the diaspora. The major provides a broad overview of the Asian American experience, including the history of immigration, the development of community organizations, and the cultural and artistic expressions of Asian American communities. The major also provides students with the opportunity to focus on specific themes and issues such as labor, gender, and the environment. Through their studies, students gain a deeper understanding of the complex forces that have shaped Asian American life and the contributions of Asian Americans to the social, political, and economic life of the United States.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Asian American and Asian Diaspora Studies

Concentration name: East Asia, Southeast Asia, and South Asia
description: The Asian Studies major offers three areas of concentration: East Asia, Southeast Asia, and South Asia. This interdisciplinary program is designed for students who want to study Asia through several different disciplines and/or more than one of the sub-regions of Asia. Students may also focus their study of Asia on a single sub-region and a single discipline. The major is designed to provide a broad understanding of the history, culture, and society of Asia, while also providing students with the language skills necessary to engage with the region.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies

description: The undergraduate major in astrophysics is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in both physics and astronomy. The major is intended to prepare students for graduate study in astrophysics or related fields, as well as for careers in industry or education. Astrophysics is the study of the physical nature of the universe. It uses the tools of physics to understand the properties of stars, galaxies, and the large-scale structure of the universe, as well as the physical processes that govern them. The major includes a comprehensive set of courses in mathematics and physics, as well as a thorough introduction to the concepts and techniques of modern astronomy and astrophysics. At UC Berkeley, we have a very active department, with approximately 30 faculty, 30-40 researchers and 100 undergraduate students. Our researchers and students have access to many world-class facilities, including the Keck and Lick Observatories, several space-based telescopes, and various supercomputing facilities.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Astrophysics

Concentration name: Biomedical Devices, Biomedical Imaging, Cell & Tissue Engineering, Synthetic & Systems Biology, Computational Bioengineering, Pre-Med
description: Bioengineering is a field that applies engineering principles and design concepts to biology and medicine for healthcare purposes (e.g., diagnostic or therapeutic). Bioengineering is a multidisciplinary field, and its goal is to bridge the gap between engineering and medicine, combining the design and problem-solving skills of engineering with medical biological sciences to advance health care treatment, including diagnosis, monitoring, and therapy. Bioengineers can be found working in a wide range of industries and sectors, including medical device companies, biotechnology companies, pharmaceutical companies, hospitals, and research institutions.
Accreditation status: The Bioengineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering

description: The joint major program in Bioengineering and Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is designed for students who are interested in exploring the interface between these two fields. Bioengineering applies engineering principles to biological systems, while MSE focuses on the design and development of new materials with specific properties. Students in this joint major will learn how to apply materials science principles to biological systems, and how to develop new materials for medical and biological applications. Students should refer to the Bioengineering and MSE departments for more information about the specific research areas and opportunities available in each field.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering - Materials Science and Engineering

description: The Management, Entrepreneurship, & Technology (M.E.T.) program is a fully integrated, two-degree program that allows students to earn two Bachelor of Science degrees in one program—combining the best of the top-ranked College of Engineering and Haas School of Business. The Bioengineering & Business Administration track gives students the opportunity to learn how to apply engineering principles and design concepts to biology and medicine for healthcare purposes. Students develop a deep understanding of the biological world and how to engineer solutions to improve human health, while also gaining a solid foundation in business principles to bring these innovations to market. Students in the M.E.T. BioE + Biz track graduate with a B.S. in Bioengineering and a B.S. in Business Administration. The curriculum is designed to be completed in four years.
Accreditation status: The Bioengineering B.S. program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET (http://www.abet.org). The Haas School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering and Business Administration

description: The Haas Undergraduate Program provides students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand the modern business world, to prepare them for specialized careers in areas such as accounting, finance, marketing, and management, and for graduate study. This program is highly competitive and provides a rigorous, broad-based education in business and the liberal arts, emphasizing core competencies such as accounting, finance, marketing, business communication, and organizational behavior.
Accreditation status: The Haas School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration

description: The Celtic Studies program is designed to give students a comprehensive overview of the history, literature, and culture of the Celtic-speaking peoples from the earliest times to the present. The program offers a multidisciplinary curriculum that includes courses in the languages and literatures of the Celtic world (modern and medieval Irish, Welsh, and Breton), as well as in the history, archaeology, and folklore of the Celtic-speaking peoples.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Celtic Studies

description: The chemical biology major provides a strong foundation in chemistry and the biological sciences. It is intended for students who want to study the interface of these two disciplines. The major is designed for students who are interested in pursuing careers in medicine, pharmacy, or the pharmaceutical industry, as well as those who want to pursue graduate study in chemical biology, biochemistry, or related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Biology

Concentration name: Biotechnology, Chemical Processing, Energy and Environment, Materials Science and Technology, Business and Management, and Applied Physical Science
description: The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE) offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Chemical Engineering. Chemical engineering is a discipline that influences numerous areas of technology. In broad terms, chemical engineers conceive and design processes to produce, transform, and transport materials — beginning with experimentation in the laboratory and followed by implementation of the technology in full-scale production. Chemical engineers are in great demand because of the large number of industries that depend on the synthesis and processing of chemicals and materials. In addition to traditional careers in the chemical, energy, and oil industries, chemical engineers are finding increasing opportunities in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, electronic device fabrication, and environmental engineering. The unique training of the chemical engineer becomes essential in these areas when processes involve the chemical or physical transformation of matter.
Accreditation status: The Chemical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering

description: The College of Chemistry and the College of Engineering offer a joint major in Chemical Engineering and Materials Science and Engineering. This program is designed for students who are interested in the design and development of materials and their chemical processing. Materials science and engineering (MSE) and chemical engineering (ChE) are closely related. Modern chemical engineering is increasingly focused on the development of materials with specific properties, such as polymers, electronic materials, and catalysts. Materials science and engineering, on the other hand, is increasingly concerned with the chemical processing of materials. The joint major program is designed for students who are interested in the synergy between these two disciplines.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering - Materials Science and Engineering

description: The joint major program in Chemical Engineering and Nuclear Engineering is designed for students who wish to prepare for careers in the nuclear power industry, nuclear research and development, or the chemical processing of nuclear materials. This joint major is one of several joint major programs offered in the College of Chemistry in conjunction with the College of Engineering. The program provides students with a strong background in both chemical engineering and nuclear engineering.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering - Nuclear Engineering

Concentration name: Methods in Chemical Biology, Computational Chemistry, Materials Chemistry
description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry is intended for students who are primarily interested in careers as professional chemists or in graduate study in chemistry. The curriculum is designed to provide a thorough foundation in the various areas of chemistry and related disciplines, and it is characterized by a wide range of rigorous laboratory and research experiences.
Accreditation status: The Chemistry B.S. degree is accredited by the American Chemical Society.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry

description: The Chicanx Latinx Studies (CLS) program offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that explores the experiences of people of Mexican and Latin American descent in the United States. The program focuses on themes such as immigration, labor, education, gender, and social movements. Through a combination of core courses and electives, students gain a deep understanding of the diverse history, culture, and socio-political dynamics of Chicanx and Latinx communities.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Chicanx Latinx Studies

description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) provides students with the linguistic and analytical tools to understand the traditions and modern formations of East Asia. The Chinese Language and Culture major introduces students to the study of the literature, history, religion, and culture of China, through its language, in its historical and regional contexts. Students can focus on modern or pre-modern (classical) Chinese, or a combination of both. Graduates with a major in Chinese go on to careers in research, education, law, medicine, government, media, arts and culture, and more.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Language

Concentration name: Engineering and Project Management, Environmental Engineering, GeoSystems Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Engineering, and Water Resources Engineering
description: Civil Engineering (CE) is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment. This includes public works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, structural components of buildings, and railways. The Civil Engineering undergraduate program at UC Berkeley starts with a focus on basic principles of mathematics and natural sciences. From these, the curriculum develops into a focus on engineering sciences and the use of the modern tools of the engineering profession. Students can then choose to specialize in one or more of the following areas: Engineering and Project Management, Environmental Engineering, GeoSystems Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Engineering, and Water Resources Engineering.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science program in Civil Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering

description: The Department of Classics offers two majors: Classics (Greek, Latin, or both) and Classical Civilizations. The former emphasizes the study of the ancient languages and the reading of the literature in the original; the latter offers a more general study of the history, literature, archaeology, and culture of the ancient world. Classical Civilizations majors develop a comprehensive and multifaceted understanding of the civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome. They take courses in many different areas—archaeology, art history, history, and literature—and also gain an introduction to one of the ancient languages (Greek or Latin).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Civilizations

Concentration name: Greek, Latin, or both (Greek and Latin)
description: The Major in Classical Languages: This major is designed for students who wish to emphasize the study of the ancient languages and to read the great works of Greek and Roman literature in the original. Students may focus on Greek, Latin, or both (Greek and Latin). The major is also suitable for students who wish to pursue a career in the teaching of Latin in secondary schools or who plan to do graduate work in Classics or a related field (e.g., Ancient History, Medieval Studies, Philosophy, or Religion).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Languages

description: Cognitive science is the cross-disciplinary study of the human mind and its processes. It examines the nature, the tasks, and the functions of cognition (in a broad sense). Cognitive scientists study intelligence and behavior, with a focus on how nervous systems represent, process, and transform information. Mental faculties of concern to cognitive scientists include language, perception, memory, attention, reasoning, and emotion; to understand these faculties, cognitive scientists borrow from fields such as linguistics, psychology, artificial intelligence, philosophy, neuroscience, and anthropology. The interdisciplinary nature of cognitive science is such that it yields a variety of areas of study at the undergraduate level.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Cognitive Science

description: The undergraduate major in Comparative Literature is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous training in literary analysis and to foster an understanding of the cultural and historical contexts in which literature is produced and received. The major invites students to study literature across national and linguistic boundaries and to explore the relationships between different literary traditions, as well as the connections between literature and other media, such as film, music, and the visual arts. Students work in at least two different languages and investigate the ways in which literary and other cultural traditions interact and overlap.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature

description: The Computer Science major is designed to provide students with a broad background in the theory and practice of computer science. Students will learn the fundamentals of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, and software engineering, as well as more advanced topics like artificial intelligence, computer graphics, and database systems. The program also emphasizes the importance of ethics and social responsibility in computer science.
Accreditation status: The Computer Science Bachelor of Arts degree is not accredited by ABET.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science

description: The Conservation and Resource Studies (CRS) major is a self-designed interdisciplinary program for students interested in environmental issues and areas of interaction among natural resources, population, energy, technology, societal institutions, and cultural values. The major's focus is on the complex problems that have arisen from the way we use and interact with the environment. Students in the CRS major design their own area of concentration (track) using courses from across the campus. These tracks have included topics such as environmental justice, global environmental politics, human health and the environment, social justice and the environment, and education and the environment. CRS students have many opportunities to explore their specific interests, through an internship and a required senior thesis project.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Conservation and Resource Studies

description: The Department of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS) teaches performance as a mode of critical inquiry, creative expression, and public engagement. Students learn to think through the body and to act through the mind. Through a diverse range of artistic traditions and theoretical frameworks, we investigate how performance shapes culture and society.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Dance and Performance Studies

Concentration name: Domain Emphasis
description: The Data Science major curriculum at UC Berkeley combines computational and inferential reasoning to draw conclusions based on data about some aspect of the real world. Data science comprises curriculum in computing, statistics, and a domain emphasis. The major is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in data science and the ability to apply those skills in a variety of fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Data Science

description: The Dutch Studies program is unique in its focus on the Netherlands and Dutch-speaking Belgium, their history and culture, and their place in the world. It provides students with a solid foundation in the Dutch language and a broad understanding of the literature, history, art, and culture of the Low Countries. Because Dutch is a Germanic language, many of the upper division courses are offered through the Department of German. However, because of its interdisciplinary nature, the Dutch Studies program also includes courses in History, Art History, and Geography.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Dutch Studies

Concentration name: Atmospheric Science, Environmental Earth Science, Geology, Geophysics, Marine Science, and Planetary Science
description: The Department of Earth and Planetary Science (EPS) offers six undergraduate majors: Atmospheric Science, Environmental Earth Science, Geology, Geophysics, Marine Science, and Planetary Science. In these majors, students learn to apply the fundamental principles of mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology to study the Earth as a system of interactively physical, chemical, and biological processes. EPS majors are designed to provide a strong foundation for students to pursue careers in research, teaching, government, and the private sector.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Planetary Science

description: The major in East Asian Religion, Culture and Languages (EARCL) is designed for students who wish to focus on the study of East Asian religion and culture. This major is more flexible than either the Chinese or Japanese major and is intended to accommodate students who wish to take a more multi-faceted approach to East Asia, and to those who wish to focus on Buddhism or some other aspect of East Asian religion and culture. The major requires at least three years of study of one East Asian language (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or Tibetan), but allows for more courses in the student’s area of interest (literature, history, thought, religion) and more of a multi-regional focus than do the Chinese and Japanese majors.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Religion, Culture and Languages

description: Economics is the study of how people and societies choose to use their limited resources. The Economics major provides students with a broad education in the field, including courses in economic theory, econometrics, and a variety of applied topics. Students learn to analyze economic issues using quantitative methods and to think critically about the role of government and markets in society. The department offers a wide range of courses in such areas as economic history, international trade and finance, labor economics, and public policy. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in economic theory and its application to a variety of real-world problems.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Economics

Concentration name: Forestry, Natural Resource Management
description: The Ecosystem Management and Forestry (EMF) major provides students with the multidisciplinary knowledge, skills, and tools to manage and bridge the conservation of complex ecosystems. Forests and other natural resources provide timber, water, habitat, and recreation. As the world’s population grows, we face new challenges: global climate change, wildfire, and an increasing need for sustainable natural resources. The EMF program provides students with the tools to solve these problems by integrating knowledge of forest ecology and biology with management of wildland resources and an understanding of the social, economic, and policy aspects of resource management. Students in the EMF major will select one of two specializations: 1. Forestry or 2. Natural Resource Management. The Forestry specialization is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF) and provides a pathway to a professional career in forestry. It is the only program in the San Francisco Bay Area that provides the necessary training to become a Registered Professional Forester (RPF) in California. The Natural Resource Management specialization is designed for students who want a broad education in the management of natural resources. It provides flexibility for students to focus on areas such as conservation, restoration, or environmental policy.
Accreditation status: The Forestry specialization is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF).
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Ecosystem Management and Forestry

description: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) program is designed for students who want to study both electrical engineering and computer science. The program offers a vibrant and innovative environment where students engage with world-class faculty and cutting-edge research. The EECS curriculum provides a well-rounded education in the fundamentals of electrical engineering and computer science, while also allowing students to specialize in areas of interest through technical electives. The EECS major is a rigorous program that prepares students for careers in industry or for further study in graduate school. It includes foundational coursework in mathematics, physics, and engineering, as well as advanced coursework in specialized areas of EECS.
Accreditation status: The Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences

description: Energy engineering is a multidisciplinary field that includes the study of energy production, conversion, storage, and consumption. The Energy Engineering program is one of several majors within the Engineering Science program in the College of Engineering. The program provides students with a strong foundation in physical sciences and engineering, with a focus on energy systems, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy policy. Students learn to analyze and design complex energy systems, considering technical, economic, and environmental factors.
Accreditation status: The Engineering Science program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Energy Engineering

description: The Engineering Mathematics and Statistics major provides students with the opportunity to study a core curriculum in mathematics and statistics along with a choice of a concentration in an engineering or science field. This interdisciplinary program provides a study in mathematics and statistics and their applications to engineering and the physical sciences. This major is intended for students who have a strong interest in mathematics and/or statistics and their application in engineering and the sciences. Students may choose from a wide variety of concentrations.
Accreditation status: The Engineering Mathematics and Statistics program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Mathematics and Statistics

description:
The Engineering Physics major is interdisciplinary and offers students the opportunity to study a variety of fields, including:
The program is designed for students who have a strong interest in physics and wish to prepare for careers in research or development in the high-technology industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in physics and mathematics, while also offering students the chance to explore a range of engineering disciplines. Students choose an area of concentration in one of several engineering departments (bioengineering, civil and environmental engineering, electrical engineering and computer sciences, industrial engineering and operations research, materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, or nuclear engineering). Graduates are well-prepared for graduate study in physics or engineering, as well as for careers in industry.
Accreditation status: The Engineering Physics program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Physics

description: The English major is designed to introduce students to the history of literature written in English and to the variety of methods by which such literature can be analyzed. It offers students an opportunity to study many different kinds of writing in English, from medieval poetry and early modern drama to contemporary novels and digital media. In the English major, students are invited to learn about the various traditions of poetry, drama, and prose; they are also invited to learn about the ways in which these traditions have been shaped by and have helped to shape the history of the world in which they were written. The department offers courses in all periods of English and American literature, from the earliest to the most recent, as well as courses in the history of the English language and in creative writing.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in English

description: The Environmental Economics and Policy (EEP) major provides a foundation in microeconomic theory and its application to environmental, natural resource, and international development issues. EEP students explore how the tools of economic analysis can be used to solve some of the world’s most pressing problems, from climate change and biodiversity loss to poverty and food insecurity. The curriculum includes courses in economic theory, quantitative methods, and environmental and resource economics.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Economics and Policy

description: The Environmental Engineering Science (EES) major is an interdisciplinary program in the College of Engineering. It is intended for students who are interested in the scientific and engineering aspects of environmental problems and their solutions. The program provides a foundation in mathematics, physics, and chemistry, and it also includes coursework in the biological and geosciences. The curriculum emphasizes the application of engineering principles to the study of the environment and is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible background. It also prepares students for graduate study in environmental engineering and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering Science

Concentration name: Biological Science, Physical Science, and Social Science
description: The Environmental Sciences (ES) major is designed to provide students with the necessary biological, physical, and social science backgrounds to analyze and solve environmental problems. The ES major is highly interdisciplinary, reflecting the nature of the environmental problems that it addresses. The curriculum provides students with a broad and rigorous foundation in the natural sciences (biology, chemistry, physics, and calculus) while also introducing students to the social sciences (economics, policy, and human behavior). Each student chooses one of three concentrations: Biological Science, Physical Science, or Social Science. Students also complete a senior research project (the ES Senior Seminar), which involves a year-long independent research project on an environmental problem of their choosing.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Sciences

description: The Ethnic Studies major provides a core curriculum designed to develop a comparative and multidisciplinary understanding of the experiences and communities of people of color in the United States and abroad. Students may also take more specialized courses on the history, culture, politics, and sociology of particular groups (e.g., African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicanx/Latinxs, and Native Americans).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Ethnic Studies

description: The Department of Film & Media offers an undergraduate major leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The program provides students with a deep understanding of the history, theory, and aesthetics of moving-image media. The curriculum explores the development of cinema from its beginnings to the present day, covering a wide range of national cinemas and genres. Students develop critical tools to analyze film as an art form and a social practice, while also exploring the theoretical and cultural implications of various media forms. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, research, and writing, and provides students with the analytical tools necessary to understand the role of media in modern society. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in film and media-related fields, as well as for graduate study in the humanities and social sciences.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media

Concentration name: Plan A (Literature and Culture), Plan B (French and a Related Field)
description: The Department of French at Berkeley is one of the top-ranked in the country, and its distinguished faculty offers a wide range of courses in French and Francophone literature and culture, from the Middle Ages to the present day. Language instruction at all levels is provided by a talented group of professional lecturers. The department's undergraduate program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the French language and in the literatures and cultures of the French-speaking world. In addition to gaining proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing, students develop skills in literary and cultural analysis, critical thinking, and research. The major also prepares students for graduate study in French or related fields, as well as for careers in education, international business, law, diplomacy, and more.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in French

description: Gender and Women's Studies (GWS) is an interdisciplinary field that investigates how gender and sexuality are shaped by and within social, cultural, historical, political, and economic contexts. The GWS curriculum at UC Berkeley offers students the opportunity to study gender and sexuality through a wide range of disciplines, including history, sociology, anthropology, literature, art, film, and media studies. In GWS courses, students learn to analyze power and inequality, and to understand how categories of difference—such as race, class, ability, and nation—interact with gender and sexuality. Students also develop critical thinking, research, and writing skills that are valuable in a wide range of careers.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Women's Studies

Concentration name: Biotechnology and Bioenergy; Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Genomics; Plant Biology
description: The Genetics and Plant Biology (GPB) major, offered by the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology, provides an undergraduate program that examines the fundamental aspects of how plants function. Students in the GPB major study the molecular and cellular biology of plants, as well as their interactions with other organisms and the environment. The program provides a broad foundation in the biological sciences, with an emphasis on plant biology and genetics. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for careers in research, education, and biotechnology, as well as for further study in graduate or professional schools.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Genetics and Plant Biology

Concentration name: Earth System Science, Economy, Culture and Society, Global Environmental Change, Urban Studies and Development
description: Geography is a diverse and active community of scholars engaged in research and teaching about the surface of the earth and the people who live on it. Geographers study the distribution of physical and social phenomena, the ways people interact with and modify their environment, and the nature of places and regions. The undergraduate major is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of the field and its core themes: earth’s physical environment, human-environment relations, and the spatial and social logic of human society. At the same time, the major is flexible enough to allow students to focus their studies in areas of particular interest, such as global environmental change, earth system science, urban studies, or economy, culture, and society.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Geography

description: The geology major is designed for students with a primary interest in the history and evolution of the Earth, including the causes of the current shape and structure of the Earth’s surface, the materials that make up the Earth, and the processes that control its long-term development. Geology is an interdisciplinary science that uses principles of physics, chemistry, and biology to explore the Earth system. Undergraduate research is highly encouraged. Graduates of this program may go into the private sector, work for government agencies, or pursue graduate school.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Geology

Concentration name: Plan 1: German Literature and Culture, Plan 2: Interdisciplinary
description: The German Department at the University of California, Berkeley, is one of the oldest and most prominent German departments in the United States. Its graduate program is consistently ranked among the top programs in the country. At the undergraduate level, the department offers a major and a minor in German. Students may focus their studies on various aspects of German language, literature, and culture, or pursue a more interdisciplinary track. The department also offers several courses in English that are popular with students from across the university. With its distinguished faculty and diverse course offerings, the UC Berkeley German Department provides students with a rich and stimulating environment for the study of German-speaking cultures.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in German

Concentration name: Global Development, Global Health and Environment, and Global Peace and Conflict
description: The Global Studies program provides students with the tools to understand the complex issues that define our world. Students choose a specific geographic region or a global theme to focus their studies. The major offers three tracks: Global Development, Global Health and Environment, and Global Peace and Conflict. Regional specializations include Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, Middle East, and Russia/Eastern Europe/Central Asia. This interdisciplinary program allows students to study how the globalization of markets, cultures, and politics affects the lives of people in different parts of the world.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies

description: The History Department at Berkeley is one of the top-ranked programs in the world. It provides its students with a strong foundation in the history of several different parts of the world and in several different periods. Students learn how to read and think critically, how to evaluate evidence, and how to write clearly and persuasively. The major is designed to be flexible, allowing students to pursue their own interests within the field.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in History

description: The Department of History of Art at Berkeley provides an excellent program for the student who wants a strong liberal arts education and a thorough knowledge of the history of art. Training in the department leads to an understanding of the relationship between art and the cultures that produced it. It also develops the student’s ability to think, to look, and to write in a clear and critical way.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in History of Art

description: Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (IEOR) is the discipline of finding and applying the most efficient and effective way to design, organize, and operate complex systems. These systems can be found in a variety of industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, finance, transportation, and energy. IEOR professionals use mathematical modeling, data analysis, and optimization techniques to improve the performance of these systems and solve complex problems. The Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the core principles of IEOR, including probability and statistics, optimization, and system design. Students also have the opportunity to take a variety of elective courses in areas such as financial engineering, supply chain management, and health care systems.
Accreditation status: The Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research

Concentration name: Plan A: Ecological, Evolutionary, and Organismal Biology; Plan B: Human Biology, Health, and Society
description: The Department of Integrative Biology (IB) offers an undergraduate major leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The IB major is designed to provide students with a broad and fundamental education in biology, while also allowing for specialization in areas of particular interest. The department's focus is on the integration of biological knowledge across all levels of organization, from molecules to ecosystems, with an emphasis on the evolution and function of organisms in their natural environments.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Biology

description: The Interdisciplinary Studies Field Major (ISF) is a research-oriented program that allows students to develop an individualized major program of study around a research problem of their own design. The major is designed for students who have a specific research interest that cannot be pursued within a single department. ISF students work with a faculty advisor to create a program that includes courses from at least three different departments. The program culminates in a senior thesis. In the thesis, students are expected to engage in a rigorous and systematic study of their research problem and to demonstrate their mastery of the multidisciplinary approach they have developed.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies

description: The Department of Italian Studies at Berkeley is widely recognized as one of the best in the country. It is dedicated to the study of the literature, culture, and history of Italy, from the Middle Ages to the present. The undergraduate program in Italian Studies provides students with a solid foundation in the Italian language and a broad understanding of Italian literature and culture. It is a multidisciplinary major that combines language study with courses in literature, film, history, and the arts, allowing students to explore the richness and diversity of Italian contributions to world culture.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies

description: The major program in Japanese is intended to provide a solid foundation in Japanese language and to introduce students to the breadth of Japanese culture and its contribution to the human experience. While students may focus on either classical or modern Japanese literature, they will also have the opportunity to study a range of other topics in the humanities, including linguistics, film and media, thought and religion, and history.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese Language

Concentration name: Korean
description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) at UC Berkeley is one of the premier centers for the study of China, Japan, and Korea in the world. Its renowned faculty and excellent students engage in the study of East Asian civilizations from the beginning of writing to the present day, across multiple disciplines. The department offers an undergraduate major with three tracks—Chinese, Japanese, and Korean—and a minor. The undergraduate program in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the languages, literatures, and cultures of East Asia. The major program requires language study and a distribution of courses in the history, literature, and culture of the region.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Korean Language

description: Landscape architecture is the design, planning and management of the land. Its objectives are to create and preserve beauty, to maintain a healthy environment, and to promote social well-being. The undergraduate curriculum in landscape architecture centers on creative and ecologically based design, and the inventory, analysis, and design of the land. It provides students with a sound general education in the arts and sciences as well as a specific orientation to the concepts and skills of landscape architecture. Through the Bachelor of Arts in Landscape Architecture, the College of Environmental Design (CED) seeks to foster an understanding of the relationship between the built and natural environments; provide students with the skills to design and manage sustainable landscapes; focus on design and planning at the site, neighborhood, and regional scales; and emphasize the importance of community engagement and social justice in landscape architecture and environmental planning. This program is a four-year non-professional degree that provides a pre-professional education, but does not qualify a student for professional licensure.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Landscape Architecture is a non-professional degree. It is not accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Landscape Architecture

description: The Latin American Studies (LAS) major provides students with a broad knowledge of Latin American history, culture, and society, as well as a specialized knowledge of a particular region or topic within Latin America. Students develop linguistic proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese and are encouraged to spend time studying or conducting research in Latin America. The LAS major is an interdisciplinary program, and its requirements include courses in several different departments.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies

description: Legal Studies is an interdisciplinary major in the College of Letters and Science that focuses on the study of law and justice. The program is designed to provide students with an understanding of the nature of law, the ways in which law is created and applied, and the relationship between law and society. The major is not a pre-law program in the professional sense, but rather a liberal arts program that emphasizes critical thinking, research, and writing skills. The Legal Studies major is based on the assumption that law is a fundamental social institution and that its study is essential to a liberal education. The curriculum is designed to introduce students to the various ways in which law can be studied, including historical, philosophical, sociological, and economic perspectives. Students are encouraged to develop their own interests within the major and to choose courses that reflect those interests.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies

description: Linguistics is the study of language as a human faculty. Its goals are to understand the structure of human languages, how they are learned, how they are used, how they change over time, and how they are represented in the brain. The undergraduate major in linguistics provides students with a solid foundation in the core areas of the field—phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics—and introduces them to the diversity of the world's languages and the methods used to study them.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics

description: The Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) department offers a comprehensive program of education and research. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong foundation in the physical and chemical sciences, as well as the engineering principles required to design and develop new materials for a wide range of applications. Students learn about the various classes of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites, and explore the cutting-edge fields of nanotechnology, biomaterials, and energy materials. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on laboratory experiences and provides opportunities for research and internships. Graduates of our program are well-prepared for careers in industry, government, and academia, and are poised to become leaders in the field of materials science and engineering.
Accreditation status: The Materials Science and Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The Department of Mathematics offers two majors: Mathematics and Applied Mathematics. The Mathematics major is intended for students who are interested in the theory of mathematics. It is suitable for those who wish to pursue a career in teaching, in government or industry, or who wish to pursue graduate study in mathematics or a related field. Mathematics is a highly developed and yet still very active subject. It has many applications in the sciences, and in many other areas as well. The undergraduate program in mathematics provides a solid foundation in the core areas of the subject and allows students to explore various advanced topics.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics

Concentration name: Aerospace Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Control, Design, Energy and Environment, Manufacturing, Materials Processing, Mechanics, Mechatronics, Micro and Nanoscale Engineering, Nuclear Engineering
description: Mechanical Engineering is the most diverse of the engineering professions, as its application ranges from the design of small parts to large-scale systems. Mechanical engineers apply their knowledge of mathematics and the sciences to solve technical problems, while also considering the effects of their work on the environment and society. Students in the Mechanical Engineering (ME) program begin with a foundation of engineering sciences (mainly physics and mathematics) and then move on to study the ME core: design, manufacturing, controls, and thermo-fluids. Students can also choose technical electives in several different areas to tailor their education to their specific interests.
Accreditation status: The Mechanical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering

description: The Media Studies Major is an interdisciplinary program in the College of Letters and Science. It is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of the role of media in society. The program provides a broad liberal arts education, focusing on the history, values, and structure of media systems and their impact on culture, politics, and the individual. Media Studies students learn to think critically about the media and to communicate effectively in a variety of forms.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Media Studies

Concentration name: Microbial Ecology and Evolution, Host-Pathogen Interactions, and Microbial Biotechnology
description: Microbes—bacteria, fungi, and viruses—are the most abundant and diverse life forms on Earth. They are essential to every ecosystem on the planet and play an integral role in human health and disease. Microbial biology is a major for students interested in studying the fundamental processes of microbial life and their applications in biotechnology, medicine, and environmental science. The program provides a strong foundation in chemistry, biology, physics, and math, while offering specialized coursework in microbiology.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Microbial Biology

description: The undergraduate major in Middle Eastern Studies (MES) is a multidisciplinary program designed to provide students with a multifaceted understanding of the history, politics, cultures, and languages of the Middle East. The major is intended to provide students with a comprehensive and multidisciplinary understanding of the Middle East as a region and the diverse cultures that inhabit it. The program includes study of a Middle Eastern language (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish) and coursework in history, social sciences, and humanities. Students are encouraged to develop a specific interest within the major, such as a focus on a particular period, country, or theme (e.g., gender, religion, or conflict).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Middle Eastern Studies

Concentration name: Biochemistry, Molecular, and Structural Biology; Cell and Developmental Biology; Genetics, Genomics, and Development; Immunology and Pathogenesis; Neurobiology
description: The Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) major focuses on the study of the fundamental structures and processes of life at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels. It is one of the largest undergraduate majors at UC Berkeley. The department is organized into five divisions: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology; Cell Biology, Development and Physiology; Genetics, Genomics, and Development; Immunology and Molecular Medicine; and Neurobiology. The MCB major provides a strong foundation in modern biology and prepares students for a wide range of careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and beyond.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Molecular and Cell Biology

Concentration name: Animal Health and Behavior, Biodiversity, Ecology, and Environmental and Human Health
description: Molecular Environmental Biology (MEB) focuses on the organization and function of biological organisms and their relationship to each other and their environment. This major focuses on how organisms adapt to different environments and explores the environmental and human health impacts of biology. MEB is particularly suitable for students who wish to emphasize the biological and health aspects of environmental science. The program provides students with a broad foundation in the biological sciences, with a focus on the study of organisms, their molecular and cellular biology, and their relationship to the environment.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Molecular Environmental Biology

description: The Department of Music offers a program of study leading to the degree of Bachelor of Arts. The major provides a base for many different careers and is particularly appropriate for students who wish to emphasize music in a liberal arts education. It also serves as preparation for graduate study in music history and literature, theory, composition, performance, or ethnomusicology. The Department of Music is an active participant in the campus’s rich cultural life. Its concerts, lectures, and other events are widely known for their number and quality. The department presents approximately 100 concerts each year and sponsors numerous seminars, workshops, and colloquia.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Music

description: Native American Studies (NAS) is an interdisciplinary program that offers a major and a minor. The NAS program provides an opportunity for students to study the history, culture, politics, and contemporary situation of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas. The curriculum is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the unique political, legal, and social status of Native American nations and communities. The program focuses on themes of sovereignty, self-determination, and decolonization, drawing on disciplines such as history, law, literature, sociology, and environmental studies.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Native American Studies

Concentration name: Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations; Middle Eastern Civilizations; Near Eastern Art and Archaeology
description: The Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures offers a major and a minor in Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures (formerly Near Eastern Studies). The major provides a comprehensive study of the languages, literatures, and civilizations of the Near/Middle East from antiquity to the present. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the history, culture, and languages of the region, while also allowing for specialization in a particular area of interest.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Near Eastern Studies

description: The Department of Nuclear Engineering offers a program of undergraduate study leading to the Bachelor of Science degree in Nuclear Engineering. The program is designed to provide a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of nuclear science and engineering. This foundation includes nuclear physics, reactor physics, thermal hydraulics, radiation detection and measurement, and nuclear materials. Students also gain experience in the design and operation of nuclear systems through laboratory courses and a senior design project. The curriculum is intended to prepare students for careers in the nuclear industry, national laboratories, or government agencies, and for graduate study in nuclear engineering or related fields.
Accreditation status: The Nuclear Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering

Concentration name: Physiology & Metabolism
description: Nutritional Sciences (NS) is an undergraduate major offered by the Department of Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST). This major provides a strong foundation in the biological and chemical sciences. In the Physiology & Metabolism (PM) track, students learn about the biology and chemistry of how our bodies utilize nutrients from the food we eat. The PM track covers topics ranging from the molecular and cellular level to the organ system level. This track is ideal for students who are interested in pursuing careers in medicine, research, or other health-related fields. In order to graduate, students must complete at least 120 units, including the university's requirements, the college's requirements, and the major's requirements.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Sciences

Concentration name: Global Peace and Conflict
description: Global Peace and Conflict provides students with the tools to understand the origins and nature of conflict, as well as the conditions for peace. This track is inherently interdisciplinary, drawing on scholarship from across the social sciences and humanities. Students explore topics such as the causes of war, the role of international law and organizations, the dynamics of social movements, and the challenges of peacebuilding in the aftermath of conflict. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical frameworks and practical case studies, encouraging students to think critically about how individuals, communities, and nations can work toward a more just and peaceful world.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Peace and Conflict Studies

description: The department offers an undergraduate major in philosophy leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad background in the history of philosophy and a basic understanding of the major subfields of philosophy. The department's faculty members represent a wide range of interests and approaches to the subject. The undergraduate major is intended to provide a solid foundation for further study in philosophy, as well as a good general education for students who plan to enter other fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy

description: The Physics major is designed to give students a solid foundation in the concepts and principles of physics. It is intended to prepare students for graduate study in physics or a related field, or for a career in industry or government.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Physics

Concentration name: Geographic or thematic area (e.g., Development and Globalization; International Trade and Finance; Science, Technology, and the Environment; or a specific region)
description: Political Economy is an interdisciplinary program that studies the intersection of politics and economics. It provides students with a sophisticated understanding of how the state and the economy interact and shape each other. The curriculum focuses on three main areas: the role of the state in the economy, the impact of economic processes on political systems, and the historical development of economic and political institutions. Students in the major explore the relationship between the individual, the state, and the market, and the ways in which these entities interact to create public policy and economic outcomes. The major is designed to provide students with a broad-based education in the social sciences, while also allowing them to focus on a particular area of interest through their concentration.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Political Economy

description: Political science is the study of politics, government, and public policy, both in the US and around the world. Political scientists seek to both describe and explain political phenomena. This includes study of the processes by which government decisions are made, the role of citizen engagement, the nature of political institutions, the causes of international conflict and cooperation, and the comparative performance of different government systems. Political Science is one of the largest majors on the UC Berkeley campus. Our faculty members’ research and teaching cover all of the major subfields of political science: American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, models and politics, and formal theory and quantitative methods.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science

description: The Psychology Department at UC Berkeley provides a program of study that is both broad and deep, including courses in the six key areas: Behavioral and Systems Neuroscience; Clinical Science; Cognitive Neuroscience; Cognitive Psychology; Developmental Psychology; and Social-Personality Psychology. Our undergraduate program is intended to provide students with a broad exposure to the different areas within the field. Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. It is a multifaceted discipline and includes many sub-fields of study such areas as human development, sports, health, clinical, social behavior and cognitive processes.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology

description: Public health is a multi-disciplinary field that focuses on health and disease at the population level. The curriculum for the public health major is designed to provide students with a broad introduction to the field of public health, as well as to the social and behavioral sciences, the biological sciences, and the quantitative sciences (e.g., biostatistics and epidemiology). The program also provides students with the opportunity to explore more specific areas of public health through elective coursework.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Public Health

description: The Religious Studies major is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the diverse religious traditions of the world and the various ways in which religion has shaped human history, culture, and society. The curriculum is flexible, allowing students to focus on a particular religious tradition, geographical area, or thematic interest. Religious Studies students develop skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural analysis, and research that prepare them for a variety of careers and further academic study. The program provides an interdisciplinary and cross-cultural approach to the study of religion, drawing on a wide variety of academic disciplines—including history, philosophy, literature, anthropology, sociology, and art history—to provide a comprehensive understanding of religion as a human phenomenon.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies

Concentration name: History and Theory of Rhetoric, Public Discourse, Narrative and Image
description: The rhetoric major offers a course of study that is at once highly focused and broadly inclusive. It is focused on the analysis and practice of discourse in its varied forms: persuasive, polemical, instructive, and aesthetic. It is inclusive because rhetorical study concerns the relation of discourse to all the conditions of human experience: the historical and the contemporary; the material and the intellectual; the social and the political; the legal and the literary. The study of rhetoric provides the student with the critical and analytical tools for understanding the ways in which various kinds of discourse—public and private, historical and contemporary—are generated, how they work, and what they do. Rhetoric as a mode of inquiry is interested in the ways in which meanings are produced and products are given meaning.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Rhetoric

Concentration name: Concentration 1: Literature/Culture/History, Concentration 2: Language/Linguistics, Concentration 3: Old Norse
description: The undergraduate major in Scandinavian is designed to give students a high degree of proficiency in the modern languages (Danish, Norwegian, or Swedish), and a solid background in the literature, culture, and history of Scandinavia from the medieval period to the present. In addition, the department offers a major concentration in Old Norse studies. The department’s offerings also include a range of courses in English translation on such topics as Scandinavian folklore, Viking-age culture, Northern European mythology, film, and the works of Hans Christian Andersen, Søren Kierkegaard, Henrik Ibsen, August Strindberg, and Ingmar Bergman.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Scandinavian

Concentration name: Russian, East European/Eurasian, West Slavic
description: The Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures offers a major in Slavic Languages and Literatures with concentrations in: Russian, East European/Eurasian, or West Slavic. The department's faculty specialize in several areas, including Russian literature and culture of all periods; Polish, Czech, and South Slavic literatures and cultures; Slavic and East European linguistics; and Armenian studies. The major is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the language, literature, and culture of their chosen area of concentration, while also offering opportunities for broader study across the Slavic world and beyond.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Slavic Languages and Literatures

description: Social Welfare is a liberal arts major designed for students who want to study the history, structure, and functions of social welfare as a social institution and who want to study the profession of social work as it is practiced in a variety of settings. The major is designed for students with three different types of goals: those who wish to prepare for graduate study in social work; those who wish to enter the labor market in a social service position after graduation; and those who want to use their study of social welfare to help them become more informed citizens and to provide a basis for future graduate study in another field. The curriculum focuses on social welfare as an institution, social work as a profession, and on the perspectives of social science as they apply to the study of social welfare. Courses are selected from several social science departments.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Social Welfare

Concentration name: U.S. Environmental Policy and Management; Global Environmental Politics; Justice and Sustainability
description: The Society and Environment (S&E) major introduces students to the main approaches and theory for understanding the relationship between society and the environment. Environmental problems are the result of many factors: political, economic, social, and cultural, as well as biological and physical. Developing solutions requires an understanding of the intersection of all these areas. Students in S&E choose one of three concentrations: 1. U.S. Environmental Policy and Management, 2. Global Environmental Politics, 3. Justice and Sustainability.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Society and Environment

description: Sociology is the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies, and how people interact within these contexts. Since all human behavior is social, the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to the hostile mob; from organized crime to religious cults; from the divisions of race, gender and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture; and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sports. In fact, few fields have such broad scope and relevance for research, theory, and application of knowledge. Sociology provides many distinctive perspectives on the world, generating new ideas and critiquing the old. The field also offers a range of research techniques that can be applied to virtually any aspect of social life: street-corner interviewing, focused case studies, clinical analysis of census data, survey research, historical analysis, and computer simulation.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology

Concentration name: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
description: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers a program of instruction in the languages and civilizations of South and Southeast Asia. South Asia includes the nations of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Bhutan. Southeast Asia includes the nations of Brunei, Burma (Myanmar), Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam. South and Southeast Asian Studies as a field involves the study of the history, society, culture, religion, and literature of these two regions.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in South & Southeast Asian Studies

Concentration name: Spanish, Portuguese, Spanish & Portuguese, or Hispanic Languages, Linguistics, and Literatures
description: The Department of Spanish & Portuguese offers a diverse curriculum that includes the language, literature, and cultures of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds. Our programs emphasize linguistic proficiency, critical thinking, and a deep understanding of the historical and cultural contexts of these regions. Students who major in Spanish and Portuguese can choose from four different tracks: Spanish, Portuguese, Spanish & Portuguese, or Hispanic Languages, Linguistics, and Literatures.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish & Portuguese

description: Statistics is the science of learning from data. It is a discipline that is concerned with the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data, as well as the effective communication and presentation of results relying on data. Statistics is a field that is vital to many other disciplines, including the biological and social sciences, medicine, engineering, business, and public policy. The Statistics major at UC Berkeley is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the theory and practice of statistics. The program includes coursework in calculus, linear algebra, probability, and statistical theory, as well as courses in statistical methods and data analysis. Students also have the opportunity to take advanced courses in areas such as machine learning, stochastic processes, and high-dimensional data analysis. The Statistics major prepares students for graduate study in statistics or related fields, as well as for careers in a wide range of industries, including finance, technology, healthcare, and government.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Statistics

description: The Sustainable Environmental Design (SED) major is the College of Environmental Design’s newest undergraduate program. It is designed for students who are passionate about the sustainable design of the built environment at all scales: from the building and the neighborhood to the city and the region. The major offers a holistic, critical approach to urban sustainability, integrating perspectives from the environmental sciences, the social sciences, and the design disciplines. Through a combination of design studios, lecture courses, and seminars, students learn to analyze and design urban environments that are more resource-efficient, resilient, and equitable. The curriculum combines studio-based design courses with courses in urban theory, environmental science, and technology. As a result, SED students are prepared to address some of the most pressing environmental and social challenges facing our cities and regions today.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Sustainable Environmental Design

description: The Department of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS) teaches performance as a mode of critical inquiry, creative expression, and public engagement. In TDPS, performance is an interdisciplinary field that includes theater, dance, and performance studies. We offer a wide range of courses in acting, directing, choreography, design, technical theater, performance theory, history, and literature. Our goal is to provide students with a rigorous and diverse education that prepares them for a variety of careers in the arts and beyond. The curriculum is designed to foster creativity, critical thinking, and collaboration, and to encourage students to explore the intersections of performance, culture, and society.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Theater and Performance Studies

description: The Urban Studies major at the University of California, Berkeley, seeks to provide students with a broad understanding of the social, political, economic, and physical aspects of cities and urban life. The major is designed to prepare students for careers in public service, urban planning, law, and business, as well as for graduate study in these and related fields. Urban Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws from a variety of disciplines to understand the complex nature of cities. Students take courses in city planning, architecture, landscape architecture, and environmental design, as well as in the social sciences and humanities. The major emphasizes the study of urban issues from a variety of perspectives, including historical, theoretical, and practical. The major seeks to introduce students to the following bodies of knowledge: historical and contemporary analysis of American and international urbanization, urbanism, and urban design and planning; the social, economic, and political factors that shape cities and metropolitan areas; the physical form of cities and its relationship to the environment; methods for analyzing and understanding urban processes and issues; and the various ways that planners, designers, and others have intervened in cities to address social and environmental problems.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies
